items.justification: Update activation and recovery is unrelated to maintaining a design and maintenance audit trail.
Communications cryptography is unrelated to risk assessment of adopted external components.
Both prevent unauthorized access to protected assets; A by requiring cryptographically sound authentication, B by requiring sensitive data be protected.
Both protect an exposed interface against malicious use; A validates what arrives at the user interface, B constrains use of the API.
Automatic update activation is unrelated to audit trails of models and datasets.
Key lifecycle management is unrelated to verifying that specified controls were implemented.
Transport encryption of personal data is unrelated to threat modelling on configuration change.
Both verify that a deployed system actually carries its intended security controls; A through user-facing checks, B through developer verification.
Both prevent reverse engineering from revealing non-public material; A credentials embedded in the binary, B model internals inferable from outputs.
Input validation is unrelated to threat modelling triggered by configuration change.
Validating inbound network input and evaluating outputs for leakage pursue different objectives.
Recording justifications for unmet recommendations is unrelated to API abuse controls.
Both prevent unauthorized parties from obtaining sensitive information; A limits what an interface discloses, B protects the data itself.
Key lifecycle management and action logging pursue different objectives.
Preventing hostile input from being acted on and preventing it from executing in memory are distinct layers of one defence against injected content.
User guidance on secure state is unrelated to sanitisation of training data and inputs.
Transport encryption and asset tracking processes share no objective.
Tamper resistance of a device identity is unrelated to external component due diligence.
Both restrict capability to what operation requires; A limits what memory contents may execute, B limits permissions granted on other systems.
Update timeliness and documentation content requirements share no objective.
Checking whether updates exist differs from planning for the case where none can be supplied.
Password generation strength is unrelated to external component due diligence.
Informing users of a required update is unrelated to assurance over external risk owners.
User guidance on secure state is unrelated to contractual flow-down to cloud providers.
Vulnerability monitoring and the required content of system documentation pursue different objectives.
Debug interface protection and asset tracking processes are unrelated controls.
Key lifecycle management is unrelated to contractual arrangements with cloud providers.
Both handle the case where a preferred control cannot be applied: A carves out the constrained device, B requires compensating controls and risk assessment.
Update verification is unrelated to asset disposal at transfer of ownership.
B's audit trail names post-deployment maintenance, the record against which A's documented remediation process operates.
User guidance on secure state is unrelated to re-testing after a major version change.
Both protect data from unauthorized access; A in transit through cryptography, B wherever sensitive data is held.
User control over update notifications is unrelated to contingency planning where updates cannot be provided.
Limiting interface disclosure is unrelated to external component due diligence.
Continuous review against risk appetite and bounded-time remediation are the detection and response halves of one risk process.
User setup guidance is unrelated to internal audit trails of models and datasets.
Debug interface protection and transparency about data handling share no objective.
Input validation is unrelated to secure deletion at decommissioning.
Brute-force resistance and justification for using undocumented components are unrelated.
Input validation is unrelated to external component due diligence.
